(a) In General.—Except as provided in subsection (b), section 202 shall apply with respect to fishing years beginning after April 30, 2010. 
    (b) Special Rule.—Section 202(3)(B) shall only apply with respect to fishing years beginning after April 30, 2012.

fable.w: This section only sets effective dates for when section 202 applies to fishing years. The tempting reading is that fishery provisions often involve regional councils or public input, but nothing in this text calls for consultation, comment, hearings, advisory bodies, or a right to sue involving any party outside the federal government. It is a timing provision, not a participation process.
fable.s: section 202 shall apply with respect to fishing years beginning after April 30, 2010

opus.w: This is only an effective-date provision: it says which fishing years section 202 and section 202(3)(B) apply to. It requires no consultation, comment period, hearing, advisory body or right to sue that would involve anyone outside the federal government. The mention of fishing years might suggest an outside-party fisheries process, but nothing in the text creates one.

qwen_chat.w: This section merely establishes the effective dates for the application of Section 202. It does not mandate any consultation, public comment, advisory committee involvement, or coordination with non-federal entities. It is a procedural timing provision, not a participation requirement.
qwen_chat.s:
(a) In General.—Except as provided in subsection (b), section 202 shall apply with respect to fishing years beginning after April 30, 2010. 
    (b) Special Rule.—Section 202(3)(B) shall only apply with respect to fishing years beginning after April 30, 2012.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that because this section references "Section 202," and Section 202 might involve participation, this section implicitly requires participation. However, this section itself only sets effective dates for the application of another statute. It does not create any new process for consultation, comment, or coordination with outside parties. It is purely a temporal provision.
